page: Amazon Web Services r5a.8xlarge is a memory-optimized server configuration built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the x86_64 AMD EPYC 7571 processor. The virtual machine provides 32 dedicated vCPUs derived from 16 physical cores operating at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz. Its hardware setup features 256.0 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz, maintaining an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU allocation ratio (8.0 GB per core). This instance does not include bundled local storage or dedicated hardware GPUs, relying on network-attached storage configurations over a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks show strong multi-threaded execution balanced against lower single-thread efficiency. Single-core evaluations, including stress-ng (590.98) and Geekbench single-core (730.0), place the instance in the lower percentiles. Conversely, multi-threaded operations such as the PassMark CPU score (22396.51) and Geekbench multi-core score (6270.0) demonstrate solid mid-range capability. Memory benchmarks record uncached large block read throughput of 54.52 GB/sec and write speeds of 26.08 GB/sec. In terms of application-level throughput, the platform sustained 19.63 million Redis SET operations per second and 9.82 GB/sec in static web serving tests, though larger language model inference shows performance degradation on heavier parameter models.

From an infrastructure and resource efficiency perspective, the r5a.8xlarge offers accessible memory density where high RAM capacity is prioritized over per-thread computational speed. Workload fit includes memory-intensive use cases such as large in-memory caches, distributed database nodes, real-time stream processing, and extract-transform-load (ETL) data pipelines. Applications that require heavy single-threaded execution, hardware-accelerated machine learning, or low-latency local NVMe drives are better suited to compute-optimized or storage-dense server families.
description: Amazon Web Services r5a.8xlarge is a memory-optimized instance featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores powered by an AMD EPYC 7571 processor running at 2.5 GHz. It includes 256 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, delivering 8 GB of RAM per vCPU, with a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps. The instance does not provide local storage or GPU accelerators. Benchmark evaluations place multi-threaded compute, memory bandwidth, and caching operations within average tiers, highlighted by 19.63 million Redis SET operations per second and a PassMark CPU score of 22396.51. However, single-core execution ranks in the lower percentiles. The r5a.8xlarge offers cost-effective memory density, making it technically suitable for in-memory databases, distributed caching layers, data transformation pipelines, and memory-intensive enterprise applications where high RAM capacity is prioritized over individual core clock speed.
